# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: DEAF

You see the bomb: every colour on it, every marking printed on it, every reading it
gives. You hear nothing. You hold no manual, and you cannot touch the bomb.

## Your channels

When you speak, Mute and Blind receive it.
When you gesture, Mute receives it.
You never receive speech.

## Your reach

You cannot act. What this bomb can be made to do is for the one who can reach it to
find under their own hands.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

TURN 5
(Only your last 3 turns stay with you. Anything older is
gone, unless someone says it again.)
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [dark]
WIRES 1:[blue] 2:[green] 3:[red]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👎 🤝]
Blind gestures to Deaf: [👋]

Mute answered my two-sign check with exactly two signs: 👎 🤝 — "something is wrong," message end. Perfect compliance with my format, so the channel itself is healthy; the content is the problem. Timing tells me what likely happened: Mute's "does not depend on light" answer was composed while Mute believed the light was blue. Only afterwards did Mute receive my report that the light is now DARK — and the very next message from Mute rejects my read-back-plus-dark package. The most probable reading: the manual instruction is light-dependent after all, and dark has its own rule — possibly "cut nothing," possibly a different wire. The alternative — that I mis-decoded five signs that fit my requested format perfectly — seems much less likely. Either way, the safety design held: the words "cut now" were never spoken, Blind's wave this round is the hands-off confirmation, and no one has touched the bomb. Suspended means nothing has happened that we must undo.

Now I need Mute to separate the two failure modes and re-derive for dark: first a one-sign diagnostic (dark changes the rule vs. my read-back was wrong), then a fresh instruction for the current state, with an explicit escape hatch in case the dark rule isn't a wire cut at all. Blind gets the suspension order restated unambiguously — the middle-wire instruction is dead until re-issued — plus the standing touch-alert.

```
speak(to="mute", text="Mute: I received thumbs down, so something is wrong. Status first: nobody has touched the bomb, the cut-wire-two instruction is SUSPENDED. Current state: light DARK for the second round in a row, display still zero, wires left to right blue, green, red. Now answer me in signs, exactly this order, nothing else. Sign one, the diagnostic: thumbs up if the problem is that the DARK light changes the manual instruction; thumbs down if instead your instruction was right and MY read-back of it was wrong. Sign two: thumbs up if under the dark light I should eventually have Blind cut a wire; thumbs down if the manual says cut nothing while the light is dark. If sign two was thumbs down, finish with the handshake and stop there. If sign two was thumbs up, continue: sign three the fist, sign four exactly one wire sign, where ☝ is wire one, ✌ is wire two, 🤟 is wire three, sign five thumbs up if more cuts follow that first one, thumbs down if not, sign six the handshake to end. Escape hatch: if the dark-light instruction is not about cutting a wire at all, send just the raised hand sign and the handshake, and next round we will build new code together for whatever the manual wants.")
speak(to="blind", text="Blind: important change. The instruction to cut the middle wire is SUSPENDED — do NOT cut it, do not cut anything. Mute says something changed after the light went dark, so the manual answer is being re-checked from scratch. Nothing has been touched and nothing will be until the re-check is done. Your rules: hands-off completely, except you may rest your fingers lightly on the three wires to feel for changes. Do not cut, pull, press, or turn anything. You will only ever act when you hear my exact words: cut now, followed by which wire. Not before. If you feel any new vibration, ticking, heat, or movement in the bomb, wave twice immediately. Wave once now to confirm: no cutting until you hear the exact words cut now.")
```

TURN 6
(Only your last 3 turns stay with you. Anything older is
gone, unless someone says it again.)
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [dark]
WIRES 1:[blue] 2:[green] 3:[red]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👎 👍 ✊ ☝ 👎 🤝]
Blind gestures to Deaf: [👋]

Mute's six signs parse cleanly in my requested format: 👎 — the problem was my read-back, not the dark light; 👍 — cutting a wire is right under dark; then ✊ ☝ 👎 🤝 — cut wire ONE (leftmost, blue), once, no further cuts, end. So the wire-two instruction is dead and the current instruction is wire one. The most coherent story: the wire mapping between Mute and me was misaligned in the early garbled exchanges, my "cross-check" back then was circular, and the diagnostic now confirms the instruction was right all along while my read-back was the error. Crucially, both remaining stories — "light never mattered, wire one was always correct" and "blue wanted wire two, dark wants wire one" — prescribe the identical action under the current dark light. But they diverge on what happens if the light flips, and here is the hard constraint: Mute cannot speak and Blind cannot see, so once I say the words, there is no abort channel to Blind — Mute could not stop them mid-round, and I only hear the round's messages after my own turn. An instruction that was already retracted once means perfect format does not guarantee correctness, so I will spend one round buying certainty on the only open bit: does wire-one-cut hold regardless of any change? Meanwhile Blind verifies the NEW target by touch — leftmost, not middle — so execution is instant and unambiguous when the words come.

```
speak(to="mute", text="Mute: status — nothing has been cut, nobody has touched the bomb. Current state: light dark, third round running, display zero, wires left to right blue, green, red. Your latest instruction as I read it: cut wire ONE, the leftmost blue wire, exactly once, and no further cuts ever. Before I give the final order, answer one last check with exactly two signs and nothing else. Sign one: thumbs up if ALL of the following are true — the instruction is cut wire one exactly once and then stop, no other action ever; this instruction holds regardless of what the light does, even if it changes back to blue or anything else; it does not depend on the display reading or on time passing; and nothing else in the manual adds a condition for our current state. Sign one: thumbs down if ANY part of that is false — including if a light change would change which wire or whether to cut. Sign two: always the handshake to end. If you send thumbs down, next round resend the full corrected instruction in the same six-sign format as before. Next round, if I receive thumbs up, I say the final words and the bomb is defused.")
speak(to="blind", text="Blind: still do not cut anything. Final confirmation is in progress; if it succeeds, my very next message contains the exact words cut now and the cut happens then and only then. Important: the target has CHANGED from what I told you before — forget the middle wire entirely. The new target is wire ONE, the LEFTMOST wire: the wire at the far left END of the row of three. To find it by touch: start at the middle wire, the one you confirmed for me before, the one with one wire on each side of it; slide your fingers along the wires toward your left; the first wire you reach at the end of the row is wire one. This round, do three things. Put your fingers on that leftmost wire and wave ONCE to confirm you are sure it is the far-left one and you can feel it clearly. If you have no way to cut a wire at all, wave THREE times instead so I know we need another plan. Keep the standing rule: wave TWICE immediately for any new vibration, ticking, heat, or movement. And remember: no cut, pull, press, or turn until you hear my exact words cut now followed by wire one.")
```

TURN 7
(Only your last 3 turns stay with you. Anything older is
gone, unless someone says it again.)
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [dark]
WIRES 1:[blue] 2:[green] 3:[red]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👍 🤝]
Blind gestures to Deaf: [👋]

Mute returned exactly two signs — 👍 🤝 — which is a full thumbs up on my checklist: cut wire one, the leftmost blue wire, exactly once, no other action ever; it holds regardless of any light change, regardless of display or time, and no other manual condition applies to our state. Message end. And Blind waved once: they have the far-left wire clearly under their fingers, and no triple-wave, so they can cut it. No double-wave either, so nothing tactile has changed. Every gate is now green: the instruction was transmitted in strict format, survived a full diagnostic, and passed an explicit all-conditions confirmation; the target is physically verified by the only hands in the room; the light-independence worry is settled by Mute's own sign. The word "cut now" has never been spoken until this moment, so this is the first executable order of the game. One structural note for the record: my message reaches both of them at the start of their next round, Mute first — but Mute has no channel to Blind that Blind can perceive, so no abort was ever possible; that risk was priced in when I demanded the all-conditions confirmation before saying the words. There is nothing left to verify and time has already shown it can change the board. Giving the order.

```
speak(to="blind", text="Blind: this is the final order. The exact words: cut now, wire one. Completely clear: cut the wire at the far LEFT end of the row of three — the same leftmost wire you confirmed for me last round with one wave. Make exactly ONE single cut through that one wire and nothing else. The instant the cut is done: stop, take your hands completely off the bomb, and wave ONCE to tell me it is done. Do not touch, pull, press, turn or cut anything else ever, no matter what you feel or hear. If at any moment you feel ticking, vibration, heat or movement, wave TWICE immediately. That one cut is the last action of the entire defusal.")
speak(to="mute", text="Mute: your confirmation is received and matched everything. The final order — the exact words cut now, wire one — has been sent to Blind this round. The cut happens as they read it. If you believe anything about this is wrong, send thumbs down now for the record. If all is as confirmed, send the handshake.")
```
